For your stir-fry, a good alternative to soy sauce that maintains the savory, umami flavor profile is coconut aminos. It is made from the sap of coconut blossoms and salt, making it soy-free and generally safer for those with soy allergies. It has a slightly sweeter and milder taste than soy sauce, so you may want to add a splash of vinegar or a pinch of salt to balance the flavor. Another option is tamari, but you must ensure it is labeled "gluten-free" and specifically "soy-free" if the allergy is severe, as traditional tamari is still made from soybeans. If the allergy is to soy proteins specifically, coconut aminos is the safest and most direct substitute for flavor and color.
